I'm looking to learn how to play guitar. I have a pretty low budget. I'm thinking anywhere from 30-80 dollars. I want an acoustic. I'd be willing to get an electric-acoustic if it's cheap. Where can I get a guitar? Do you have any recommendations of which guitars I should get?

If your budget really is 60 bucks your best bet is to go to a flee market and buy one second hand.

EDIT: I should clarify a bit more.

You can find acoustic guitars for 60 dollars but they will be of such low quality that you would be lucky if that thing will stay in tune after 10 minutes of playing.

You will have better luck going to various flee markets to find a used one that is of decent quality.

Tips for looking for a decent guitar:

1) Make sure the tuning knobs are tight. There should be zero play in them. This is usually a moot item because the tension of the strings will prevent them from moving, but if the pegs are shit, sure, the piece that the string threads through may be solid, but if the knob is loose, the play could losen the string, or it could rattle.

2) Check if the neck is bent. Hold the guitar up and look down the neck. if you see the neck bend in any direction, you are going to have problems later on.

3) Check the hight of the frets. If the frets are too high (or the strings too low) you will hear a rattling from the strings because they are hitting the frets. If the strings are too low that might indicate that the neck bolt is too tight which causes the neck to bow. Acoustic guitars typically have a wider gap between the strings and frets than with electric guitars, but at the same time, if you see a quarter of an inch of space, thats too much and something could be bent.

4) Check the pegs that the strings get looped on at the bottom. If they look like they are being yanked out, chances are that the previous owner over tightened the strings. This could cause a problem by loosening even more, which would cause the strings to go out of tune. Or, they could come flying off.

These are the general things to look for. I won't go into what types of wood was used, what glue was used, etc. All of that plays into the quality of the guitar but for your price range you won't have to worry about that.

Also, since you are going to use it to learn on, if you find a guitar that someone is selling for 100 bucks, let's say, and it has some of these problems I pointed out, you can easily talk them down to 60 or 50.

I learned on a squire strat 15 years ago. However I never got very good playing electric. I only truly fell in love with guitar playing when I bought a musty old classical Yamaha from some dudes lawn sale.

Now I haven't even dusted off the strat in 3 years, and I still play my classical every single day.

I found learning chords, etc, on an electric MUCH harder than on the classical. Maybe it depends on what music you plan on playing. Also I highly doubt he'd find a stratocaster + amp for less than $100.

I bought a beat up musty old Yamaha from the 60's at a yard sale for $20 about 10 years ago. I spent another $50 at the local music store to buy new tuning pegs/knobs, and also replaced the nut and bridge. The new pieces didn't fit perfectly so I had to drill two new holes in the head.

I planned on sanding and refinishing it as well, but ended up just cleaning it really thoroughly. I found the small bits of damage and wear just give it more character, and they don't effect sound quality.

I just checked the sticker inside, and it is specifically a Yamaha G-65-1. I googled it and found one for sale on E-bay for $125 in mint condition. It is a classical acoustic (nylon strings from G down) and they just have a beautiful sound.

I personally think a classical is the best way to learn. If you learn on a classical, you can play electric or acoustic with ease, and they just sound so much nicer on their own.

EDIT: If you're buying BRAND NEW, anything less than a few hundred dollars will be absolute garbage. Old Yamaha's from the 70's/80's are so much better value. New is NOT better than used.
